question: How many tonnes of rare-earth permanent magnets will China export to the United States in August 2026?

calls.reasoning: Reference class: the 16 monthly China->US rare-earth permanent-magnet (85051110) volumes since the April 2025 licence regime began; these run from 0 t to ~650 t with a median near 460 t, and two outright zero months (Sept 2025, May 2026). Prior anchored at ~460 t before news. July 2026's ~647 t was the second-highest post-control month and the first above the 2024 monthly average since Oct 2025, so simple mean-reversion pulls August down even absent shocks; the one prior Aug/Jul pair (590 vs ~619 in 2025) was also modestly lower. Against that, Reuters (Sept 4) reports a handful of Chinese suppliers refusing US shipments since early August after Beijing sanctioned the Responsible Business Alliance — specific, in-window, and negative — but it is explicitly partial ('Reuters was unable to determine the total number', four cited instances), its concrete volume examples are yttrium/gallium rather than magnets, and finished magnets are the category that has been recovering while controlled compounds stay suppressed; some firms also reported newly granted licences. Offsetting upside: Trump's 200% tariff threat and summit-driven uncertainty create a real incentive for US buyers to pull shipments forward, and August tonnage reflects licences issued before the pullback. I therefore centre modestly below July with a wide, left-skewed distribution: meaningful mass at 100-300 t if the pullback bit broadly, and ~15-20% above July's level if it did not touch magnets. Evidence is thin on the magnet-specific impact, so I stay close to the reference-class centre rather than pricing the news as a collapse.
calls.dossier:
SUBJECT: tonnes of Chinese rare-earth permanent magnets (Chinese customs subheading 85051110, NOT the broader 6-digit HS 8505.11) exported to the United States during calendar month August 2026.

RESOLUTION INSTRUMENT: resolves off GACC destination-level monthly customs data for subheading 85051110 as reported by Reuters/Bloomberg/SCMP/CNBC — not off the 6-digit HS 8505.11 total, not off US import statistics, not off global magnet export totals. Where outlets differ, the most commonly cited value governs. GACC publishes headline trade data around the 8th of the following month and detailed by-destination/by-commodity data around the 18th-20th; the August 2026 detail is therefore due mid-to-late September 2026. If GACC stops publishing destination detail for the category, the question annuls.

EVENT WINDOW: 2026-08-01 -> 2026-08-31 per the criteria; as of 2026-09-07T21:20Z, 100% elapsed. The physical quantity is already determined; only its publication is pending.

STATUS-QUO OUTCOME: absent any shock, the month lands in the band the series has occupied under the licence regime, near its post-control central tendency, with July's level as the immediately preceding observation.

BASE RATES / SERIES HISTORY (all GACC-derived):
- Over the ~16 months since the April 2025 controls began, monthly US-bound volumes have spanned 0 t to roughly 650 t. Two of those months were exactly zero: September 2025 and May 2026 (question background, citing GACC).
- Conditional on the preceding month being at or above the 2024 monthly average, the sample is thin — July 2026 was the first such month since October 2025.
- Over July->August specifically, the one comparable post-control pair: August 2025 ~590 t vs July 2025 ~619 t (a ~5% month-on-month decline). Source: SCMP/Reuters reporting of GACC data.
- July 2026 US-bound: ~647 t, +32.6% month-on-month and +4.5% year-on-year, second-highest monthly volume since controls began, and the first month above the 2024 monthly average since October 2025 (Reuters/gulfnews, Silverado Policy Accelerator dashboard updated 2026-08-31, rareearthexchanges 2026-09-01). Implied June 2026 ~488 t.
- January+February 2026 combined: 994 t, -22.5% year-on-year; US was China's third-largest magnet buyer at 9.2% of total exports (SCMP, 2026-03-20).
- Cumulative January-July 2026 US-bound magnet exports ran roughly 16% below the same period of 2024 (question background). Residual arithmetic implies March and April 2026 each in the low-400s t.
- China's global magnet exports July 2026: 5,375.1 t, -4.9% month-on-month, -3.6% year-on-year; H1 2026 global magnet exports were at record levels (GACC via Reuters/digitimes).

EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD LOWER AUGUST VOLUMES:
- Reuters, 2026-09-04: a handful of Chinese suppliers have refused to ship rare earths to US customers since early August, after Beijing sanctioned the US-based Responsible Business Alliance; the firms fear punishment for complying with the Responsible Minerals Initiative audit framework. Reuters cited four instances and stated it could not determine the total number of affected suppliers. Not a formal blanket ban.
- Same Reuters piece: suppliers indicated they intend to keep commercial sales cautious until the Xi-Washington bilateral talks scheduled for 2026-09-24 conclude.
- China added 10 US entities to its dual-use export-control list on 2026-06-22, including MP Materials and USA Rare Earths, with immediate effect (S&P Global).
- Elevated bilateral tension during the window: Trump publicly threatened tariffs of up to 200% if China curbed magnet supply.
- Controlled rare-earth compounds and metals to the US remain far below historical levels; total rare-earth transfers to the US run at roughly half 2024 levels (Chinese customs data cited by Reuters).
- MOFCOM has banned export of rare-earth extraction, separation and magnet-manufacturing technology outright.

EVIDENCE POINTING TOWARD HIGHER OR UNCHANGED AUGUST VOLUMES:
- The commodities named in the September 4 supplier-refusal reporting were yttrium, gallium, terbium, tungsten and indium phosphide — raw and refined inputs — not finished sintered NdFeB magnets. The article carried no magnet tonnage impact estimate and did not quantify aggregate August disruption.
- Same article: some US firms reported recently receiving multiple licences after long waits.
- Analysts note China's restrictions have bitten far harder on separated compounds and metals than on finished magnets, which have been rebounding (rareearthexchanges, 2026-09-01; Silverado, 2026-08-31).
- Shipments in any month reflect licences and orders placed weeks earlier, so a pullback beginning in early August has a lagged and partial effect on August-dated customs entries.
- Tariff threats and visible supply risk create an incentive for US buyers to accelerate orders and stockpile.
- Silverado notes China is on average shipping physically smaller sintered NdFeB magnets to the US, so unit counts and tonnage can diverge; the resolution metric is tonnage.

SEARCHED FOR BUT NOT FOUND: any published or preliminary August 2026 US-bound magnet figure (GACC detail not yet out as of 2026-09-07); a complete month-by-month 2025-2026 US-bound tonnage table (CSIS, Silverado and MacroMicro pages did not expose one — MacroMicro and one trade-data aggregator returned HTTP 403); any magnet-specific quantification of the supplier pullback; any exact 2024 US-bound monthly average figure; any prediction market, bookmaker or exchange contract on this quantity on Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold — none found.

calls.reasoning: Reference class: the 15 monthly China->US NdFeB magnet volumes under the post-April-2025 licensing regime (GACC subheading 85051110). Trailing-12-month mean is ~490 t, and the Feb-Jul 2026 mean is ~476 t; that is my prior, not July's 647 t. July 2026 (647.3 t, +32.6% MoM, highest since Oct 2025) is an outlier at the top of the post-control range, and this series reverts hard after spikes: after Jul 2025's ~619 t came 590 t then 420.5 t; after the Oct 2025 peak came five consecutive monthly declines to a 406 t nine-month low in Mar 2026. Straight mean reversion alone puts August near 520-580. Adjusting down for the documented shock: MOFCOM listed the Responsible Business Alliance on 5 Aug 2026 and Reuters (4 Sep) reports a handful of Chinese suppliers have since refused US shipments, covering ~85% of the August month. But the reporting is thin and mostly about non-magnet materials -- Reuters quantified yttrium (27 t in July), not magnets, cited only four documented refusal instances, and could not size the total; major magnet makers hold general licences and the customs figure partly clears June/July orders, so the hit is partial and lagged. The RMI due-diligence channel does bite disproportionately at US automotive/electronics buyers, which is the main downside mechanism and why my distribution is left-skewed. No market prices this. Upper escape (>1200 t) is priced at 1%: no month in the entire series, including pre-control 2024, has approached that level.

- 2025: May 46 | Jun 352.8 | Jul ~619 (implied by July 2026 being +4.5% YoY) | Aug 590 (-5% MoM) | Sep 420.5 (-28.7% MoM) | Oct = local peak, above 647 and above the 2024 monthly average

- Jan-Jul 2026 cumulative is roughly 16% below the same period of 2024.

BASE RATES / DISPERSION:
- Over all 15 post-control months (May 2025 - Jul 2026): mean ~470 t, range 46-750 t.
- Conditional on the licensing regime having normalised (Nov 2025 - Jul 2026, excluding the May-Jun 2025 shutdown): mean ~490 t, range 406-647 t.
- Conditional on the six most recent months (Feb-Jul 2026): mean ~476 t.
- Conditional on the three most recent months: mean ~536 t, direction upward.
- Month-over-month log changes, Nov 2025 - Jul 2026: SD ~0.18 (observed MoM moves -18%, -9.5%, ~-4%, +21%, +3%, +33%). Including the May-Jun 2025 shutdown months the SD is ~0.28.
- Post-spike behaviour in this series: the two prior local peaks (Jul 2025 ~619, Oct 2025) were each followed by declines, one mild (-5%) and one steep (-28.7%), then a multi-month downtrend after October.
- Global monthly magnet exports, Jul 2026: 5,375.1 t, -4.9% MoM, -3.6% YoY. Mar 2026 global: 5,238 t. Q1 2026 global: 16,001 t, +4.8% YoY. EU was the largest destination bloc in July 2026 at 39.8%; Germany led individual destinations; the US ranked second, ahead of South Korea.

EVIDENCE POINTING DOWN:
- 5 Aug 2026: MOFCOM placed the Responsible Business Alliance and five other US supply-chain due-diligence entities on its Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law countermeasure list, five days after the US added 43 Chinese firms to the UFLPA Entity List on 31 Jul 2026 (Morrison Foerster, 21 Aug 2026; Fieldfisher; Kumi). Chinese mineral companies were urged to halt all RBA/Responsible Minerals Initiative audits, data submissions and cooperation (MLex).
- Reuters, 4 Sep 2026: a handful of Chinese suppliers have refused to ship rare earths to US companies since early August, wary of Beijing punishing them for complying with RMI due diligence; some held valid export licences. Sources cited four specific instances of Chinese firms declining to send material. Other Chinese rare-earths firms had already stopped US shipments in recent months to avoid geopolitical entanglement.
- 22 Jun 2026: MOFCOM blacklisted MP Materials and USA Rare Earth, barring Chinese firms from supplying them dual-use materials.
- Some US firms have waited more than six months for mineral licences; prices for yttrium, indium phosphide and tungsten remain near record highs on tight supply.
- RBA/RMI frameworks are used chiefly by automotive and electronics buyers, which are the dominant end-users of US-bound NdFeB magnets.

EVIDENCE POINTING UP:
- The Reuters halt story is scoped to rare earths broadly; the only tonnage it quantifies is yttrium (27 t to the US in July, second-highest month since Jan 2025, after two zero months). It does not name magnet producers, does not report any magnet tonnage, and states Reuters could not determine how many suppliers were involved.
- General export licences (one-year, client-specific) were rolled out to major magnet makers: JL Mag can ship to nearly all its customers; Ningbo Yunsheng and Zhong Ke San Huan hold narrower permissions; suppliers to Ford received them.
- Reuters' own framing is that exports of many rare earths and related magnets have rebounded since the April 2025 restrictions.
- Customs clearances in early August reflect orders and licences from June/July, so a halt beginning 5 Aug propagates only partially into the August figure.
- Xi visits Washington on 24 Sep 2026; rare-earth supply is on the US planning agenda and some firms anticipate an increase in licence approvals around the summit.
- US buyers face documented stockpiling incentives given repeated supply interruptions.

DATA-QUALITY NOTE: the question background states US-bound magnet exports were zero in May 2026. Sources found contradict this -- the zero applies to export-controlled rare-earth compounds and metals; US-bound magnet exports in May 2026 were 473 t. Treat the 473 t figure as the magnet series value.

calls.reasoning: Reconciled on evidence, not by averaging the runs. The load-bearing fix is factual: the 'zero in May 2026' in the background is the controlled rare-earth compounds/metals series, not magnets - US-bound magnets were 473 t. Internal arithmetic confirms it: with Jan+Feb 994, Mar 406, Jun ~488, Jul 647 and Jan-Jul 2026 ~16% below Jan-Jul 2024, a zero May would force Apr and Jun near 800 t each, contradicting July's 647 t being the highest month since Oct 2025; May = 473 closes the arithmetic and implies a 2024 monthly average of ~580-600, itself consistent with July being the first month above that average since Oct 2025. So there is no zero month in this series since June 2025, and the deep left tail one run priced is unsupported. Prior is therefore the stable 2026 run-rate of ~470-500 t, not July's outlier 647 t. Two forces pull below July: ordinary reversion after a licence-catch-up spike (the one in-regime Jul->Aug pair moved -5%; the Oct-25 peak was followed by five straight declines), and the 5 Aug RBA listing with Reuters' 4 Sep report of suppliers refusing US shipments despite valid licences. That shock is real but partial and lagged - Reuters quantified only yttrium, cited four instances, could not size the total, major magnet makers hold general licences, and August clearances partly discharge June/July orders - so it justifies left skew, not a step change. Centre 490 t, about 0.76x July.
calls.reconciliation: In dispute: (1) whether US-bound magnets were 0 t in May 2026 (Run 1, following the background) or 473 t (Runs 2 and 3); (2) how much the RBA-sanction supplier pullback cuts August magnet tonnage; (3) how far to revert from July's 647 t. No web access this run, so (1) was settled by arithmetic consistency across figures all three dossiers agree on - a zero May is irreconcilable with Jan-Jul 2026 running ~16% below 2024 while July at 647 t is the highest month since Oct 2025, whereas 473 t fits cleanly. I therefore adopt Runs 2/3's corrected series and reject Run 1's zero-inclusive reference class and its 105 t p10; that is why my centre is above Run 1's 460 t and my left tail much thinner. (2) is pure judgment that no dossier resolves - Reuters explicitly could not determine how many suppliers were involved and quantified no magnet tonnage, while RMI adopters are exactly the auto/electronics magnet buyers, so I price it as a partial drag with a fat-ish left tail rather than a regime break; I would bet on partial. (3) I carry Runs 2/3's reference-class prior (~470-500 t 2026 run-rate) forward as my own, with July treated as an outlier. My 490 t centre sits marginally below their 500 t because I weight the in-window pullback slightly more than they did, and my 90-10 width of 425 t sits between Run 3's 400 and Run 2's 470. Publication timing (GACC detail due ~18-20 Sep vs a 19 Sep scheduled resolution) affects when, not what, resolves - the fine print waits on delayed data. No human market prices this quantity; the harness's Manifold candidates are unrelated and were not used.
